added_lines: . Forty Hours Adoration for the Solemnity of Christ the King in the Cathedral, Mullingar from Friday 20th to Sun. 22nd Nov. The Sacrament of Reconciliation will be available from noon to Midnight on Sat 21st. Each parish in the Diocese has been invited to spend one hour in Adoration before the Blessed Sacrament. Our parish hour is Sunday 22nd, 3 - 4pm . Adoration will conclude with Solemn Vespers & Benediction at 4pm on Sunday led by Bishop Deenihan, with Bishop Fintan Monahan as Homilist. Kilbeggan

Pope Leo’s prayer intention for November - For the proper use of wealth Let us pray for the proper use of wealth, that not succumbing to the tempt ation of selĮshness, it may always be put at the service for the common good and solidarity of those who have less. See Pope’s video and transcript/prayer on our parish website

Each and every one of us must respond to the Lord by saying, “Thank you for the talents you have given me! I want to use them for the good of all. ” It is likewise also up to each of us to say to our neighbour, “You are a brother or sister to me. Let us cultivate together the talents that bear fruits of a good life for this city, our country and the future of justice and peace we wish to build. ” This commitment is summed up in a gesture we make during Holy Mass, when we bring to the altar the fruits of the earth and of human labour. The table that the Lord prepares draws us into an exchange of gifts that we present to God so that we may then share them with the world. In the light of the Gospel, I invite you, then, to multiply the talents the Lord has entrusted to you by cultiva ting three speciĮc things. Above all, cultivate your faith together. Be a people who celebrate God’s salvation and heal the wounds of humanity. Indeed, the Church uses human words to speak God’s truth; and she preaches the word of God to proclaim the truth about the human person. Following the example of Christ, the Word made Ňesh, we can observe everyday reality with the wisdom that comes from the Gospel, opening up a future of righteousness for all. This mission begins in prayer and is nourished by the sacraments. The work of the whole Church is carried out in families and parishes, in the streets and schools, in hospitals and prisons. Seek to multiply the Lord’s gifts everywhere, promoting communion with all men and women of good will. Second, I encourage you to cultivate the grandeur of our humanity. This commitment applies above all to young people, who are the hope of the Peruvian people. It likewise applies to caring for children and protecting the elderly, as well as to solidarity with the poor and the oppressed. Doing good requires combating violence with charity and responding to corruption with honesty. Where people are healed, the earth Ňourishes, and the culture of charity alleviates moral pollution — which is the cause of every wound inŇicted on creation, our common home. Finally, in the face of every trial, always cultivate joy. Christians know that this joy does not come from wealth or power, which degrade us like a drug, deceiving the heart and le aving it in anguish. True joy comes from faith, because it is founded on God’s grace, which bears fruit in our fraternal self-giving. As we go through tribulations and challenges, let us build together a happy, pea ceful and free society, gazing upon the Lord Jesus, who bestows peace from his Cross, taking upon himself each of our diĸcul ties. Let us ask him, the Redeemer, to accompany us on our journey, giving us the light of hope. May his Mother Mary, the Immaculate Virgin, always comfort and protect you. The Charity ‘Aid to the Church in Need’ calls on all of us to join them in pr ayerful support for all who suffer for their faith.

The Candle in November We light a candle as a sign of remembrance.
We make a little offering and we say a Prayer for that person, that they may be enjoying the light of heaven.
The candle reminds us that we too have the opportunity to share the light of hope that we carry with others.
When you are in a dark place the warmth of a smile or a kind word can mean a lot.
May the light of Christ shine for all to see as the Gospel reminds us keep our lamps lit.
